clue.text: Most affordable parrot in box

indicators.note: in places the word for parrot within the word for box

parts.note: a chest is a box
to parrot or ape is to mimic

explanation.surface: A pet shop advertises its bargain bird sold in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' looks like the bird but is the verb meaning to copy, and the copied word is split by the box around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapest is the superlative of cheap, costing the least money, so the most affordable.

clue.text: Social class describing Liberal MP for Blackburn

indicators.note: describing is used in its sense of drawing round, so the class word encloses the letter

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social class

explanation.surface: A politician's class background is described in a profile of the Liberal member for a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Castle was the Labour MP for Blackburn, Lancashire, from 1945 to 1979, so 'Liberal' is only a letter, not her party.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara Castle, a Labour cabinet minister, represented the Lancashire town of Blackburn in Parliament for decades.

clue.text: Back no EU changes with grace

indicators.note: changes tells us to alter the order of the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A call to support turning away from the European Union, done gracefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two pieces of fodder; NOEU and GRACE together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To back someone is to support or hearten them, which is what encouraging does.

clue.text: Drink editor slugged

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink

explanation.surface: A drink-fuelled newspaper editor hit someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' and 'slugged' both suggest alcohol; slug here is to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To slug someone is to strike them hard with the fist, the same as punching them.

clue.text: Put up with French writer penning last bit of script

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds animals, so the writer's name goes round the letter

parts.note: George Sand was a French novelist

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Tolerating a French author who writes the end of a script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, fitting the writer, but means enclosing: SAND goes round T.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate or endure it, the idiom put up with.

clue.text: Rubber gloves idiot initially kept in chap's room

indicators.note: kept in says the initials are held inside the word for chap

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Rubber gloves belonging to some fool are stored in a man's bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'room' is space to spare, not a chamber; the 's after chap is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is leeway or spare space, as in room for error.

clue.text: Assumed American chose to support Democrat

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: opted means chose

explanation.surface: An American voter decided to back the Democratic candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue OPTED goes below A + D.
explanation.definitionFit: An adopted name or manner is one taken on as one's own, i.e. assumed.

clue.text: Naive novelist ignoring conclusion

indicators.note: ignoring conclusion says the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist

explanation.surface: An unsophisticated writer who never finishes a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Green describes someone inexperienced or gullible, a common figurative sense of the colour.

clue.text: Around noon, son seen cooking tripe

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the single letter for noon
cooking means the letters are being worked up into something new

explanation.surface: At midday a son is spotted preparing offal.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripe looks like the offal being cooked (stomach lining eaten as food), but here it means rubbish talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is a colloquial word for worthless talk or writing, a synonym of nonsense.

clue.text: Forged rod nicely pulling out old engine part

indicators.note: forged means made or fashioned, so the letters are reworked
pulling out says a letter is removed from the fodder before the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A rod has been neatly forged, but an old engine component is being removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O out of RODNICELY and rearrange what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The cylinder is the chamber in which a piston moves in an internal combustion engine.

clue.text: Inferior new school

parts.note: secondary means of lesser importance, inferior
modern means new

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on some newly opened school.
explanation.walkthrough: A secondary modern was the British state secondary school for pupils who did not pass the eleven-plus exam to enter a grammar school.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a type of state secondary school in Britain for children not selected for grammar schools.

clue.text: Left with a sound of disgust and Edward chuckled

parts.note: ugh is an exclamation of disgust
Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Edward walked off grunting in disgust, though he was actually laughing.
explanation.definitionFit: To chuckle is to laugh quietly, so chuckled is a mild form of laughed.

clue.text: Major's hip? Stiff

parts.note: hip means fashionable, which is in
stiff muscles are tense

explanation.surface: A sergeant major complains of a stiff hip.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Major' is a link word (is). 'Major' looks like the army rank but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means great in degree or very strong, as major pain is intense pain.

clue.text: Got sidetracked and we ordered wine

indicators.note: ordered here means put into a new sequence, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: red is wine

explanation.surface: We lost focus and asked for a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like asking for the wine, but it rearranges AND WE into WANDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander is to stray from a path or topic, so wandered means drifted off the point.

clue.text: Backlash concerning lawsuit

parts.note: re means concerning, about
an action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Public backlash over some legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction, especially a hostile one, is a backlash against an event or decision.

clue.text: Sailors might leave these details?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: harbour ..., places sailors depart from

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags 'details' as de-tails: to dock an animal is to cut its tail short.
explanation.definitionFit: Docks are harbour berths for ships, and docking is cutting short an animal's tail.

clue.text: Bishop might be seen in this red hat manufactured in California

definitions.text: Bishop might be seen in this

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the abbreviation for the state
manufactured means made up, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A churchman's red hat made in California.
explanation.walkthrough: The red hat suggests a cardinal's headwear, but the words are only letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral holds the bishop's throne, so it is the church where a bishop is often found.

clue.text: Daughter is sitting on flower? Catastrophe!

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece sitting on another sits above it

parts.note: the aster is a garden flower

explanation.surface: A daughter sits on a flower and crushes it, a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a sudden great misfortune, which is what disaster means.

clue.text: Is concealing most of sweetheart's thoughts

indicators.note: concealing means the word is goes around the shortened term of endearment
most of means one letter is lost from the end

parts.note: dear is an endearment for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: Someone hides most of what their lover is thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'sweetheart' is only a link word, not part of the endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are notions or concepts formed in the mind, so thoughts.

clue.text: Fish below ship going round each beach?

indicators.note: going round has the ship's letters enclose the abbreviation for each

parts.note: SS is short for steamship
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Fish swim beneath a ship circling every beach.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'below' puts IDE after SEAS. The question mark marks seaside as a loose definition for beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaside is the coast where people go for the beach, an example-style definition.

clue.text: Adult crowds half ignored barmy circus performers

parts.note: A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: half ignored means only the first half of the word is used

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy, barmy

explanation.surface: Adult audiences shunned half the crazy people performing in a circus.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of CROWDS is CRO. Barmy is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobats perform gymnastic feats such as tumbling and trapeze work in a circus ring.

clue.text: Food picked up with reduced fat — it's criminal

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts a word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: grub is slang for food

indicators.note: reduced means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: Low-fat food is described as a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: GRUB written upwards gives BURG, and LARD cut short gives LAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar breaks into buildings to steal, so is a criminal.

clue.text: Remained respectable on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard over the airwaves, signalling a word that sounds the same

parts.note: staid means sober and respectable

explanation.surface: A broadcaster stayed decent on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain in place, so stayed is the past tense synonym of remained.

clue.text: Pull cat's tail after a stretch

indicators.note: after says the cat's last letter follows the a
tail means the final letter of the word

parts.note: a tract is a stretch of land

explanation.surface: Yank the cat's tail after it has a stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'cat' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw towards oneself, the same as exerting a pull.

clue.text: Aquatic birds reportedly go south

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: to go south is to worsen, which is what milk does when it turns

explanation.surface: Seabirds are said to fly south for winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go south' looks like migration but is the idiom for going bad: turns. Terns are seabirds.
explanation.definitionFit: Terns are slender seabirds that dive into water for fish, hence aquatic.

clue.text: Dog tore present

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
rent is a past tense of rend, to tear

explanation.surface: A dog ripped up a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but is the adjective, existing now.
explanation.definitionFit: Current means belonging to the present time, as in current events.

clue.text: In hutch I'm petting animal

indicators.note: In says the answer lies within the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone stroking an animal kept in a hutch.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimp, short for chimpanzee, is an ape and therefore an animal, a definition by example.

clue.text: Soldiers annoyed at military error

indicators.note: annoyed means stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Troops angered by a blunder made by the army.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was Britain's volunteer reserve force of part-time soldiers, now the Army Reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The Territorial Army was a British reserve force made up of part-time volunteer troops.

clue.text: Breads regularly provided with the woman's slice of bacon

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word, starting from the second

parts.note: her means belonging to the woman

explanation.surface: A woman's breakfast of bread and bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is a thin strip of bacon or ham, cut for frying.

clue.text: Box with a thousand large eastern diamonds glittered

parts.note: to spar is to box
K stands for a thousand
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A box holding a thousand big eastern gems shone brightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container but is the verb, to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkled means shone with flashes of light, much as glittered does.
